title: ‘Spirit of the Photobooth’ Doc Highlights the Invention’s Democratic Origins and Its Gen-Z Resurgence
full_text: × Skip to main content By Caitlin Huston Plus Icon Caitlin Huston Business Writer hustonca Follow Sign Up View All November 16, 2026 11:26am Add us as a Google Preferred Source A group of young women waiting to use a Photo Booth machine at Gatwick Airport in East Sussex, England on 14th June 1963. Len Trievnor/Express/Hulton Archive/Getty Images In honor of the 100th anniversary of the humble photobooth, a new documentary unveils its democratic origins, its place in history as means of self-expression and its recent resurgence among Gen-Z. The documentary, entitled Spirit of the Photobooth , played an encore screening at the International Center of Photography Saturday as part of the inaugural Art Week from Artforum and ARTnews. The film, written and directed by Sam Anthony, first premiered in September. As told in the film, Anatol Josepho, a Russian immigrant to the U.S., founded the automated analog photobooth as a means for everyday people to be able to get their own portraits, instead of the more expensive and time intensive process of sitting for a studio photo. The first photobooths were located just north of Times Square and caused a sensation in 1926, with crowds lining up for a chance in the booth until 4 a.m. The next year Josepho sold the patent for the booths for $1 million to businessman Henry Morgenthau, who launched booths across the nation. From there, photo booths popped up at army bases, allowing soldiers to send home a photo, and expanded into Europe, where they were favored among members of the surrealist movement. The automated, private nature of the booths also gave Black Americans a chance for self-expression in the Jim Crow South, and gave queer couples an opportunity to take home private keepsakes, with some photobooths stationed in men’s bathrooms. Andy Warhol used photobooth strips as a basis for his pop art and silk screen painting, helping to legitimize it as a form of art. While photobooths gradually fell into disuse, due to the rise of digital cameras and cell phones with cameras, a dedicated group of enthusiasts across the globe have worked to bring old booths back to life — the refurbishment is pricey, but the business of booths is quickly profitable — and to revive enthusiasm for the practice. Happily, Gen-Z has since flocked to photobooths — with one owner noting it may be “some of the only analog tech” they’ve experienced — as enthusiasts say they’re in search of something tangible and real, and have seen the locations promoted on social media.The Old Friend Photobooth in lower Manhattan is one of the most popular current locations, with the Gen-Z owners now turning their attention to refurbishing a booth at Coney Island, the former mecca for photo booths from the 1940s through ‘70s. title: Ella Langley Brings Country Into The Grammys’ General Field With Seven Nominations
full_text: × Skip to main content By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All November 16, 2026 11:25am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ella Langley Jason Kempin/Getty Images Unless you’ve been living under a rock or have never set foot in any retail store, Ella Langley ‘s chart-topping country anthem “Choosin’ Texas” has been unavoidable over the last year. The wildly catchy track, co-written by country icon Miranda Lambert, launched Langley into a new league, which was reflected in the 2027 Grammy Awards nominations . The 27-year-old was tied for the third-most nominated artist of the year, with seven nominations, four of which are in the general field categories. Langley earned nods for best new artist, album of the year, song of the year and record of the year, along with best country song, best country solo performance and best contemporary country album. Through “Choosin’ Texas,” Langley’s represented in all general field categories, with collaborators Miranda Lambert and Joybeth Taylor getting nominated for producer of the year and songwriter of the year, non-classical. Related Stories Music Grammy Nominations Snubs and Surprises: Harry Styles, Madonna, Noah Kahan Miss Top Nods as Raye, Rosalía Overperform Movies Lady Gaga and Doechii's "Runway" Is Sole 'Devil Wears Prada 2' Song Oscar Submission (Exclusive) Released in October 2025, “Choosin’ Texas” has continued to dominate on the charts. The track, currently sitting at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, has spent 27 weeks atop the chart, making it the longest-running song to accomplish such a feat. Langley is the only country artist nominated in the four major categories — album of the year, song of the year, record of the year and best new artist. Coming into the year, it was unclear whether or not the singer would even be eligible for the best new artist category. Historically, artists could only submit to the category three times, which Langley had already hit. However, the Recording Academy announced that they’d be expanding the category to allow four entries per artist, making her eligible. THR

title: Gwen Stefani Will Celebrate Orange County Roots by Performing at Grand Opening of OCVIBE’s 5,000-Seat Concert Hall This Spring
full_text: × Continue to Variety SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Breaking News Robert Pattinson Is the New James Bond Nov 16, 2026 11:22am PT Gwen Stefani Will Celebrate Orange County Roots by Performing at Grand Opening of OCVIBE’s 5,000-Seat Concert Hall This Spring By Chris Willman Plus Icon Chris Willman Senior Music Writer and Chief Music Critic ChrisWillman Latest Grammy Nominations 2027: Raye Leads With 11 Noms as Rosalía, Olivia Rodrigo, Ella Langley and Other Female Artists Dominate 8 hours ago Phoebe Bridgers’ Skeletal Transformation on ‘SNL’ Wasn’t Just a Startling Special Effect — It Emotionally Elevated One of the Best Pop Songs Ever Written About Death 19 hours ago Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Ceremony Gets Fired Up With Live-Wire Numbers From U2, the Chili Peppers, Usher, Cynthia Erivo, Sienna Spiro, Aerosmith and More 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Gilbert Variety Gwen Stefani used part of her induction speech for Billy Idol at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony Saturday night to recall how she used to listen to the rocker on the bus on the way to Huntington Beach. She’ll be returning to Orange County to do what counts as a hometown show in March, opening a high-profile new venue in Anaheim that is part of the OCVIBE complex. Perhaps her limo driver can turn on some Idol on the way to the show. The 5,000-seat venue at which Stefani will serve as the grand opening attraction is the OCVibe Concert Hall, one of several entertainment destinations that are planned for the $5 billion, 100-acre district. Her show there will take place March 17, OCVIBE reps announced Monday. Related Stories Nicolas Cage Says 'I'm a Little Bit Homeless' and 'Living in Hotels' After Sinkhole at His House ‘Lords of War’ Trailer: Nicolas Cage and Bill Skarsgård Star as Father and Son in ‘Lord of War’ Sequel “My roots are in Orange County, so it’s such an honor to be the first artist to perform at this incredible new venue OCVIBE,” Stefani said in a news release. “It’s really special to be part of this exciting opening and to celebrate with the community that means so much to me.” Not that many rock stars have proudly proclaimed Orange Country as their point of origin, but Stefani has embraced it since the early days of No Doubt in the ’90s. In 2024, she attended a ceremony to be inducted into the Orange County Hall of Fame’s inaugural class. Tickets for her solo show go on sale via a Live Nation presale on Thursday at 10 a.m., via a sign-up for the venue’s Encore Club presale list to the general public, here. A general public onsale will follow beginning Friday at 10 a.m. PT at ticketmaster.com . The Concert Hall is expected to draw in artists who might otherwise play venues in L.A. like the Greek. The March 17 opening will be part of a year that will see other parts of the complex open, including the Katella Commons food hall and public plazas, with more development set to come going all the way into at least 2030. “Having Gwen Stefani come home to Anaheim to open OCVIBE’s Concert Hall is an incredibly special moment,” said CEO Bill Foltz in a statement. “Gwen is an artist whose roots are deeply connected to this community, and we couldn’t imagine a more meaningful way to introduce OCVIBE’s Concert Hall to Orange County. Her performance will be the first opportunity for the community to experience a piece of what we’ve been working toward, and a preview of the music, culture, dining, and experiences that will bring this district to life. We can’t wait to welcome everyone.” Also in the works for the complex is a 300-capacity music club that is being named the Golden Bear, after a venerable but long-gone club that used to be a cornerstone of the Orange County music scene in Huntington Beach. The Concert Hall will take up the middle spot between that intimate club and the nearby Honda Center, which is reported to be getting an upgrade as part of the OCVIBE opening. title: Justin Long & Kate Bosworth To Headline Indie Comedy Series ‘The Renovation’
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News New James Bond Found: Robert Pattinson To Play Next 007 Read the full story By Denise Petski Denise Petski Senior Managing Editor More Stories By Denise ‘3 Body Problem’ Sets Season 2 Release Date At Netflix Dolly Parton Earns Three Posthumous Grammy Nominations ‘Beast Games’ Sets Season 3 Release Date At Prime Video View All November 16, 2026 11:18am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Justin Long, Kate Bosworth Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: The resurgence of independent television series continues to grow with Justin Long ( Barbarian, You Deserve Each Other ) and Kate Bosworth ( Still Alice, Along for the Ride ) starring in The Renovation , a fully-financed indie comedy series. It hails from Lucas Carter ( Summer of ’69) , Nick Kreiss ( Punk’d ) who directs all episodes, Intrigue , Script2Screen and Hammerstone Studios . Production has wrapped in Los Angeles, and EPs Intrigue, Script2Screen and Hammerstone will begin shopping the series to streaming platforms and television networks this month for distribution. Related Stories Acquisitions Hulu Buys Animated TV Comedy Pitch 'Detective Agent Derek' From Nick Kreiss, Trio Big Grey Mass Acquisitions Emile Hirsch, Justin Long & Kevin Connolly Pic 'Lice' Acquired By Bob Yari's Magenta Light Studios - Cannes Blending scripted comedy with hidden-camera elements, The Renovation centers on a real, unsuspecting married couple, played by real-life married duo Long and Bosworth, who believe they are participating in a home renovation television show. What they are unaware of is the contractors, fellow contestants, and everyone around them are actors, following a carefully constructed storyline designed to test the couple’s instincts, decision-making and sense of right and wrong. Watch on Deadline Conceived by writer and producer Carter, The Renovation takes a fresh approach to the hidden-camera format, combining the storytelling and structure of a scripted comedy with the unpredictable reactions of real people. The concept for The Renovation was originally developed by Carter, who brought the idea to Tariq Jalil’s Intrigue, Carter’s former employer, where the pair further developed the project. The series is executive produced by Jalil, Carter, Kreiss, Alex Lebovici, Ibrahim Mohammed, Yasmyne Mohammed, Chase Vergari, Michael Mazzarra, along with Long and Bosworth. Dan Swimer, Oscar-nominated screenwriter for Borat Subsequent Moviefilm , also serves as an executive producer. Long and Bosworth are repped by Independent Artist Group and Yorn Levine. title: Grammy Nominations Snubs and Surprises: Harry Styles, Madonna, Noah Kahan Miss Top Nods as Raye, Rosalía Overperform
full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All November 16, 2026 11:16am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Harry Styles, Rosalía and Noah Kahan Jason Kempin/Getty Images; Gilbert Flores/Billboard/Getty Images; Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images It was less than four years ago that Harry Styles won the Grammy for album of the year, but he won’t get a chance to defend his title or win another Grammy this go around for his latest album Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally , as he was completely shut out of the 2027 Grammy nominations . Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally was a bit more sonically complex than Styles’ past album of the year winner Harry’s House , and heading into this year, Styles was widely looked at as a Grammy contender for his latest release, which debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 album chart while lead single “Aperture” hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. Neither the album nor the single had the same staying power as Harry’s House or its lead single “As It Was,” though he gave the album more buzz with a 30-show Madison Square Garden residency as part of his Together, Together tour. Evidently, it wasn’t enough to sway the Grammy voters. Related Stories Movies Lady Gaga and Doechii's "Runway" Is Sole 'Devil Wears Prada 2' Song Oscar Submission (Exclusive) Music John Summit Blasts Grammys After Dance Snub: "It's All a F***ing Joke" Other surprise shutouts this morning include Gracie Abrams , who wasn’t nominated for her third album Daughter From Hell , which hit No. 1 on the Billboard 200, and Hilary Duff, whose comeback record Luck … Or Something , for new label Atlantic Records , was released in February and debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard 200. While Abrams scored a best new artist nomination in 2024, it’s not her first time getting the Grammys ‘ cold shoulder, also failing to land expected song and record of the year nods last year for “That’s So True.” Others were lucky enough to score nominations but maybe not as many as pundits (or fans) had expected. Noah Kahan landed just one nomination, for best contemporary folk album, for his The Great Divide , despite a number of experts predicting the former best new artist nominee would score top nods for his latest effort. “Life goes on,” Kahan tweeted on Monday . And while Madonna ‘s Confessions II was an eagerly awaited follow-up to 2005’s Confessions from the pop superstar and landed her four nominations , the release failed to net the seven-time Grammy winner any nominations in the major categories, including album, record and song of the year. For anyone else, five Grammy nominations is an incredibly impressive feat, but even though that’s how many nods superstar singer-songwriter Taylor Swift received Monday — with noms in all three of the general categories — it’s perhaps an understated showing compared to what we’ve come to expect for the world’s biggest artist. Speaking of superstar musicians, Paul McCartney was left out of the major categories for his latest release The Boys of Dungeon Lane , which only landed one nomination, for best traditional pop vocal album. But the former Beatle did land three nominations, two of which were for Morgan Neville’s Man on the Run documentary about McCartney’s departure from the iconic group. Kanye “Ye” West continued his comeback with an unexpected Grammy nomination for best rap album for his latest release Bully , as the controversial rapper aims to move on from years of antisemitic comments. Meanwhile, both Raye and Rosalía were looked at as contenders for some of the top prizes heading into announcement day, but few would’ve expected they’d be the most-nominated acts across the whole field. Raye’s 11 noms and Rosalía’s nine were some of the best surprises for two of the year’s most ambitious projects. Other surprises include a handful of artists who landed nods despite not releasing an album during the most recent Grammys eligibility period. Beyoncé released one song, “Morning Dew (Donk),” on July 4 , as part of the 20th anniversary edition of her 2006 album B’Day and netted her 100th Grammy nomination . Similarly, Sabrina Carpenter scored two nods, albeit both in the same category of best pop duo/group performance, for her collaborations with Swift and Madonna. THR

title: Louis Carr Exits as BET President
full_text: × Skip to main content By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All November 16, 2026 11:11am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Louis Carr Paras Griffin/Getty Images Louis Carr has exited BET less than one year after he was named president. Carr was with the brand for 40 years. “I’m deeply grateful to Louis. For four decades, he has been one of BET’s greatest champions, helping shape the brand, its business and its connection to Black audiences and culture,” George Cheeks, co-chair and chief content officer for Skydance TV, wrote in a memo shared with staffers (and obtained by The Hollywood Reporter on Monday.) “Louis built lasting partnerships with some of the world’s leading brands and helped cement BET as a cultural force. As President, he led BET with clarity and purpose, creating renewed momentum for the brand. His passion, vision and heart have been front and center in everything he does, and it has been a privilege to partner with him.” Related Stories Movies James Gunn Says "No One From Skydance Has Seen" 'Man of Tomorrow,' Addresses "Untrue Rumors" Over 'Superman' Sequel Business HBO Max-Paramount+ Bundle Targeted by Subscribers in Lawsuit Challenging Megamerger Cheeks says Skydance “believe(s) deeply” in BET and “are committed” to its future. Carr’s tenure will officially end when 2026 officially ends. It was Carr’s decision to exit, Cheeks says. Skydance acquired BET with its Paramount merger, which closed last summer. Carr was named BET president in December 2025. “We will have more to share soon on BET leadership and structure,” Cheeks wrote on Monday. Carr’s farewell email, like his tenure, was lengthy. Read his message in full below. Dear Team, For 40 years, I have had one of the best jobs in the media and entertainment industry. Having a position that gives one the opportunity to carry out a purpose that is bigger than oneself is a privilege. Working for a brand whose mission from day one was to uplift and empower the Black community is an honor I’ll never forget. That said, even as I write this email, I wrestle with my decision that the time has come to make a transition. Based on recent events within our community and our country, I’ve decided to chart a new path and my last day will be December 31. BET has never been just a job to me. It has been a community, a culture and a place to serve. When I reflect on this journey, I am incredibly proud of what we have accomplished together. Over the years, we helped transform the multicultural advertising landscape, built meaningful relationships with some of the world’s most recognized brands and served as the launching pad for today’s top Black creators. We demonstrated the undeniable value, influence, and purchasing power of Black consumers while helping companies better understand and invest in our communities. I am particularly proud of the momentum we have created and the work we have undertaken to strengthen the brand, expand our business and reaffirm BET’s place at the center of Black culture. Stepping into the role of President gave me the opportunity to see just how much the BET brand is loved by our talent, our consumers and the next generation. We established our brand positioning as “Something You Can Believe In,” reinforcing the trust, purpose, and cultural connection that have always defined BET. We established a trusted Board of Advisors, one that would be envied by any Fortune 500 company, to help inform our direction and ensure that the voices and perspectives of our community remain part of the conversation. And that was just the beginning. In 2026 alone, we: Delivered the network’s highest television and digital ratings since 2019, with the 2026 BET Awards hosted by Druski. Brought back the Soul Train Awards after a three-year hiatus. Expanded our relationships with an impressive roster of Black creators such as Kev on Stage, Nick Cannon, Jason Lee, Manny Halley, Desmond Scott, Chris “CP” Powell, Ice Cube’s BIG 3, Kevin Frazier and Stephen A. Smith with HBCU Basketball and more. Expanded the global reach of Black content through multiplatform partnerships with creators such as Tyler Perry and Ms. Pat. Entered new content sectors and explored new ways to connect with audiences across platforms with the launch of our microdramas. Relaunched the iconic ComicView franchise. Launched a new social impact campaign “Get Your Mind Right,” focused on mental health to further support the communities we serve. Created a new financial model for programming spend that makes our content more aligned and efficient to our potential ratings. And so much more. The work of this incredible BET team has afforded me the opportunity to earn an abundance of professional accolades and recognition, including five Lifetime Achievement Awards, induction into the American Advertising Federation’s Advertising Hall of Fame, and more than 14 community awards. I have also been privileged to sit on board seats across the industry, including with the International Radio and Television Society (IRTS), the Advertising Council, and the American Advertising Federation (AAF). Additionally, I am proud to be the longest-serving board member of the Video Advertising Bureau (VAB). Thank you for your partnership, your commitment, and, most importantly, for allowing me to be part of your journey. It has been one of the greatest honors of my life. I am proud of what we have built and proud of what we have accomplished. With gratitude, Louis THR

title: A “Bad Call” Or “Can’t Wait”? Industry & Media React To Robert Pattinson’s Casting As James Bond

title: Mo Brings Plenty Hopes Real-Life Inspired ‘Marshals’ Episode Brings Justice to Late Nephew
full_text: Skip to main content By Jackie Strause Plus Icon Jackie Strause Managing Editor, East Coast jackiedstrause Follow Sign Up View All November 16, 2026 11:03am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Mo Brings Plenty (left), here with Luke Grimes and Ash Santos in the 'Yellowstone' CBS spinoff 'Marshals.' Fred Hayes/CBS ©2026 CBS Broadcasting, Inc. All Rights Reserved. Logo text Mo Brings Plenty, his family and community have been rocked by the untimely death of Mo’s nephew, 1923 actor Cole Brings Plenty. The 27-year-old was found dead in April 2024 after he had been reported missing . His death came between seasons one and two of the Yellowstone prequel, sparking his recasting ( with Jeremy Gauna ), a final season that honored his memory and now, an entire episode of Marshals inspired by what happened. In Sunday’s episode of Yellowstone ‘s hit CBS spinoff following Kayce Dutton ( Luke Grimes ), titled “Roughstock,” Mo, an enrolled member of the Lakota Nations who plays the right-hand man to Broken Rock Tribe chief Thomas Rainwater (Gil Birmingham) in both Yellowstone and Marshals, searches on horseback with Kayce (Grimes) for Mo’s missing nephew (played by Will Strongheart), only to eventually find him dead, and a police department refusing to investigate the death. Related Stories TV Michelle Pfeiffer and Kurt Russell Tease Major "Twists" in Season 2 of 'The Madison' TV Luke Grimes Wasn't Sure If 'Marshals' Would Be a Hit. Now He's Prepping for a 'Yellowstone' Kind of Run The storyline is ripped from what Mo believes happened to his real nephew. In Cole’s case, the Lawrence Police Department in Kansas found no foul play involved, ruling that Cole acted alone and took his own life. Mo hasn’t stopped pushing a different narrative ever since. “For his murder to go uninvestigated, and for it to be written off as ‘no foul play,’ because they didn’t want to invest anything into it? It’s heartbreaking,” he had told The Hollywood Reporter back in March . “We’re not letting it go.” Now that the episode has aired, Mo, who also works behind the scenes as the show’s American Indian Affairs coordinator, talks again with THR below about the bravery of the Paramount Taylor Sheridan series and Marshals showrunner Spencer Hudnut to spotlight Cole’s story on television, the emotions around reliving the tragedy of his nephew’s death, and the justice he hopes the episode can help bring to murdered and missing Indigenous people. “This is for the injustice that occurs to American Indian people and the victims who are truly victims, who are being being labeled otherwise and not being taken seriously,” he says. *** This must be heavy for you, so thank you for speaking with me about the making of this episode inspired by your late nephew. Did you approach (showrunner) Spencer Hudnut about doing this, or did Spencer approach you? It all began when my brother, Joe, Cole’s father, and I were sharing the experience of what we were going through. Spencer mentioned something about it being up to us. Saying, “I know it’s gonna be deep, and it’s hard. But it’s up to you.” We said, we have to do it. Not just for the sake of remembrance or in honoring Cole, but for all the other cases, all the other families whose cases of their loved ones not being looked at or being taken seriously and just thrown away. It was very important. And I knew it was going to be doable because the cast and crew are an amazing group of people. They all understood and had the knowledge of what we’ve experienced and gone through. Did you have to pitch this to the studio or network to get them on board? I think that was on Spencer. Mad respect for Spencer; even doing so, is very important. Did you talk to Taylor Sheridan about how to handle putting this storyline into the show? No. I knew exactly what I wanted to do. My biggest thing was that I wanted to relay the true emotions and spirit of it all, even the frustrating moments. Because it’s a roller coaster ride, and it still is today. It’s still fresh in our minds, my family’s minds, especially my brother Joel. He struggled. It was truly, truly a great loss for us. Spencer wrote this episode. Did you collaborate? Yes, he wrote it, and Spencer and the writing team are a great group of amazing, beautiful human beings. My brother and I went to the writers room early on, before the season even started, to spend a day with them. We talked about different things that go on within tribal councils, the political side of what goes on on a reservation, the non-political side of it and then, of course, we shared our experience of not talking about the MMIW (Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women) and MMIP (Missing and Murdered Indigenous People), but actually conveying what it’s really like to have that experience. There are hundreds and hundreds of families who have their loved ones… murdered and missing; the disappearance of loved ones just being written off as nothing. From my previous conversations with you , this episode is very close to what you believe happened to your nephew in real life. What was it like for you to film this beat by beat , playing an uncle who loses his nephew? [ Note: In the end of the episode, Kayce’s team pushes for the police to investigate the death, opening up the storyline to continue .] It was about doing justice. But it was also good to have Luke Grimes there, and Gil Birmingham, and the crew; individuals who understood and knew. Will [Strongheart], who portrayed [Mo’s onscreen nephew] Troy, was very familiar. He came to Cole’s funeral; they all knew what we were going through, especially for me. So it was easy to fall back into that space, because I knew there were others who would be there to help me if I needed it. But at the forefront of my mind was the injustice that occurs to American Indian people and the victims who are truly victims who are being being labeled otherwise and not being taken seriously. Mo’s late nephew, Cole Brings Plenty, hree as Pete Plenty Clouds in the Yellowstone prequel series 1923 , season one. Emerson Miller/Paramount+ This is a big platform: Marshals is a mega-hit for Paramount. You will shine a light on this happening everywhere, but do you hope it moves the needle specifically with your nephew’s case? Unfortunately, the way I see it, if a police department doesn’t want to investigate something then there’s a connection. Bottom line, hands down. Outside of that, what I hope this episode achieves is that it will drive people who are non-Native, who are unfamiliar, to go down this journey. We mentioned MMIW, MMIP, in the past — murdered and missing Indian women and people. But to actually have a storyline that will hopefully have the audience see it through Mo’s, Kayce’s, Rainwater’s eyes? Just to be able to actually see what is going on. The positive side in this story is that law enforcement actually does get involved — the marshals, but not the police. There’s a line where the sheriff said, “Ah, this happens all the time.” I’m glad Spencer included that line because that’s really, honestly, what a lot of families hear from law enforcement when when their loved ones are found. After we spoke the last time, the Lawrence Police Department responded to our interview with a statement . Did you see what they said? [“ The entire case contains clear evidence that there was no foul play involved in Cole’s death and that Cole acted alone .”] Oh, yeah, of course. Out of respect for my family, I encouraged my brother, Joe, to seal the records. Little did we know that it was going to give them an out. Nonetheless, I’m hoping that this episode is going to drive people to reach out to their Congress people, their senators, their governors, and say, “Hey, look, enough. Here’s the original inhabitants of this country, and here’s our treatment to them.” But yet we speak about other nationalities in foreign countries, so we’re basically flying over mission fields to get to mission fields. We want to be the savior there, but we’re not doing it here. That’s the thing that upsets me the most, and the fact that we are tax paying people as well. First responders get their funding through tax dollars. We are forced to pay taxes, and the will of justice does not turn for us? Shame on America for that. I’m being honest. And if that’s the case, then we shouldn’t have to pay taxes. If there’s no equality and justice being served for our loved ones who are truly victimized? What occurred in Cole’s case, there were allegations. And they let go the people they should have interviewed to get the true answers. If the police department really doesn’t want to investigate, then to me, that’s every bit of proof that there’s something to hide. This episode included a ceremonial burial. You have worked behind the scenes to bring authenticity to this franchise for years as the American Indian Affairs coordinator. What did you especially want to show here as Mo was laying his nephew to rest? The sacred fire… the true celebration and understanding of life. When we look at life from a spiritual perspective, it is continuous. There is no end. So that was important, because we incorporate a lot of that understanding or tradition or ceremony into our everyday lives, whether we’re assisting a family that lost a loved one or, or even ourselves, losing relatives. The spirit is forever. One of the biggest parts of that ceremony scene was the horse. Because we’ve always had horses here in this country long before the Spanish brought theirs. The Lakota people, we have songs and ceremonies specifically for the horse that are thousands upon thousands of years old, so to have that incorporated was very important to me. To share that bit of knowledge and understanding that our people have always had, that the horse symbolizes the spiritual realm. So when Mo sees that horse, he knows his nephew made it home. Is there anything you want to say about Cole in his memory? If people truly believe there’s a higher power, then they have to stand up for what’s right. Regardless of what it is. My nephew, Cole, has always done that. He was a lover of life. He always gave a helping hand. He never judged anyone for who they were, what nationality, what their faith was. If someone needed help, he was there. And to turn that type of light out in a community, in this world… for us, he was the next one to carry on our traditions and knowledge. To strip us of that and do nothing about it? If people truly believe in a higher power, they better understand and know that it is the higher power who loves diversity. Because the higher power made it so from the very beginning. And if you can’t support that diversity here, this world, on this planet, then who are you to believe you’ll be welcome there? In Marshals , the death of Mo’s nephew sounds like an ongoing story that will open up the show to explore more reservation stories, which is something Spencer Hednut said is baked into the series. There are many stories very similar to this. Different situations and circumstances, but the outcome’s always the same. I wanted to get this message out but I had to utilize our own story, my family’s own experience. I’m hoping down the road this will give us the ability for us to be able to share more; other things that are occurring. Not always the negative things. There are positive things as well, and I want to share those too. I’m hoping people will go ahead and support stories about Indian country. Do you feel like this was a brave thing by the show, the network, the studio to allow you to tell such a personal story? I’m thankful to the network for giving us the opportunity. I’m thankful to the Spencer. I’m thankful that they’ve allowed us to be able to share this experience and bring it to light through the episodes. It does take great courage, because a lot of people don’t understand cultural diversity. They don’t fully understand that we as American Indian people are tax paying people, too. Like I said, we pay bills just like everyone else. We have to work for everything that we have. I’m thankful to the network and to Spencer and to the rest of the writers who supported the whole storyline. *** Marshals releases new episodes Sundays at 8 p.m. on CBS and Paramount+. THR

title: Harlan Coben’s ‘The Innocent’ Lands Greenlight At Netflix As Streamer Strikes Overall Deal With StoryMath

Coben is back with limited series The Innocent , marking his 15th adaptation for Netflix. The streamer has greenlit the project, after Deadline revealed it was in development earlier this year. The Innocent reunites Coben with Robert Hull, showrunner of I Will Find You , which starred Sam Worthington. Related Stories Agencies ‘I Will Find You’ Showrunner Robert Hull Launching Production Company StoryMath With Steven Lilien & Bryan Wynbrandt News ‘Myron Bolitar’ Netflix Series From David E. Kelley A Go As Streamer Extends Deal With Harlan Coben Hull launched production company StoryMath earlier this year with Bryan Wynbrandt and Steven Lilien, who created CBS’ God Friended Me , and the company has now signed a new overall deal with Netflix. Watch on Deadline Interestingly, The Innocent has already been adapted by Netflix as Spanish series El Inocente in 2021. The book follows Matt Hunter, who served nine years in prison after innocently trying to break up a fight-and ending up a killer. Now nine years after his release from prison, his innocence long forgotten, he’s an ex-con who takes nothing for granted. With his wife Olivia pregnant and the two of them closing on a house in his hometown, things are looking up. Until the day Matt gets a shocking, inexplicable video call from Olivia’s phone. And in an instant, the unraveling begins. A mysterious man who begins tailing Matt turns up dead. A beloved nun is murdered. And local and federal authorities–including homicide investigator, Loren Muse, a childhood schoolmate of Matt’s with a troubled past of her own–see all signs pointing to a former criminal with one murder already under his belt… Matt Hunter. Unwilling to lose everything for a second time, Matt and Olivia are forced outside the law in a desperate attempt to save their future together. Hull, Wynbrandt and Lilien will serve as showrunners, writers and exec producers with Coben and Ben Coben serving as exec producers through Final Twist Productions. The news comes six months after Coben extended his deal at Netflix, which came to life at the streamer in 2018 with the adaptation of Safe . It was followed by British series The Stranger , Polish adaptation of The Woods , the Spanish adaptation of The Innocent , the French adaptation of Gone for Good , Poland’s Hold Tight and Just One Look , the British series Stay Close, Fool Me Once, Missing You, Run Away, and U.S. series I Will Find You. Next up, is a British adaptation of The Woods and a U.S. adaptation of Myron Bolitar from David E. Kelley and Kyle Long. Netflix’s Head of UCAN Scripted Series Jinny Howe told Deadline earlier this summer that Coben “really understands his audience” and the partnership has been “very, very successful for us”. Cole Galvin, Netflix Vice President of Drama Series, who was promoted last month , said, “Harlan Coben is one of the great creative partnerships at Netflix, and The Innocent marks our 15th story together. Nobody builds a can’t-look-away thriller like Harlan, and Robert Hull, Bryan Wynbrandt and Steven Lilien brought their own incredible creativity to I Will Find You , a global hit for us. We’re thrilled to welcome them to the Netflix family, and we can’t wait for the world to get hooked on their Innocent .” “We’re thrilled to call Netflix our home and couldn’t be more grateful to our friends Jinny Howe, Cole Galvin, James Flannery, Mike Azzolino, and of course, the incredible Harlan Coben, for their continued partnership,” added Hull, Wynbrandt and Lilien. “Bringing I Will Find You to life and seeing it connect with audiences around the world was an amazing experience. We’re excited to bring our signature brand of twisty and propulsive storytelling to The Innocent and the many new stories we look forward to telling at Netflix.” StoryMath is represented by CAA and Range, with Lilien and Wynbrandt represented by attorney Todd Rubenstein and Hull represented by attorney Dave Ryan. Books On Television Book adaptations at Netflix are clearly working. The company noted that Coben’s I Will Find You , which was published by Grand Central Publishing, saw a 500% increase in sales after the announcement of the show. Elsewhere, The Whisper Man , which starred Robert DeNiro, saw a similar increase in sales, Remarkably Bright Creatures saw sales across all formats rise 560% from its first-look launch to its peak in May, East of Eden , published by Penguin Classics, hit the number one on Amazon’s best sellers list some 74 years after publication with a 200% rise in sales and Little House on the Prairie helped drive 110% more sales for the Storytide and HarperCollins-published book. On screen, book adaptations account for nearly 20% of total view hours and over 13B global views since 2025, per the streamer. The company was at the Texas Book Festival this weekend for the first time with a panel featuring The Hunting Wives author May Cobb and Guarding Stars author Katherine Center as well as Virgin River showrunner Patrick Sean Smith and exec Cole Galvin. “People come to comfort and heartland stories for connection and optimism—the kind of story you put on to unwind. Those titles have drawn more than a billion views on Netflix since 2023, and they’ve reached viewers in more than 90 countries,” added Galvin. “But what matters most to me are the readers who loved these books first. We work with authors and creators to honor what made the stories special, and then we invite new fans in. title: In Choosing Robert Pattinson, Bond Producers Have Taken the Safe Bet — But Is It the Right One? (Opinion)
full_text: × Continue to Variety SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Breaking News Robert Pattinson Is the New James Bond Nov 16, 2026 10:32am PT In Choosing Robert Pattinson, Bond Producers Have Taken the Safe Bet — But Is It the Right One? (Opinion) The star of 'The Drama' and 'The Odyssey' caps off a massive year by winning the highest-profile casting contest in ages, but it's hard not to wonder if he really needs this. By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest In Choosing Robert Pattinson, Bond Producers Have Taken the Safe Bet — But Is It the Right One? (Opinion) 35 minutes ago ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’ Review: Indian Mythological Blockbuster Is an Eye-Popper, but Skip the English Edit 4 hours ago ‘Hen’ Review: A Resilient Chicken Flies the Coop, Over and Over, in an Unexpectedly Stirring Survival Story 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Amazon MGM So much for the underdog. After the race to be the next James Bond was reported to be down to three on-the-rise Brits — Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner — Robert Pattinson crashed the conversation late in proceedings, hugely pulling focus in a matter of days. Why wouldn’t he? Suddenly, a competition of next-big-things had a bona fide already-big-thing in the mix. 40 years old and known to multiplex audiences for almost half that lifetime, the Londoner is a household name who, even by his established standards, has been enjoying a banner year at the movies: sharing in the blockbuster glory of Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” this summer, sandwiched by inspired star turns in two offbeat A24 projects, “The Drama” and “Primetime,” that both impressively overperformed at the box office. All that, and he’s still got “Dune: Part Three” coming up next month. Related Stories Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues Adding James Bond to his roster feels almost like gilding the lily, which is one reason I was skeptical that he’d ultimately be picked: Wasn’t the announcement of Pattinson (along with Nicholas Hoult) as a contender just a glittery distraction to juice up public interest in a lower-profile selection process? Shows what I know. In picking Pattinson as the next 007, the 64-year-old movie franchise is heading into unprecedented territory: Bond has traditionally been a star-making role, not one for a readymade movie star, and that has worked out more often than not. (George Lazenby, it simply wasn’t meant to be.) Sean Connery had played just one leading role before he was cast in 1962’s “Dr. No”; prior to donning the tux, Roger Moore and Pierce Brosnan had both found their signature roles on TV. Timothy Dalton, a reasonably seasoned and well-regarded actor when cast as Bond, never quite made the leap to stardom via the role; Daniel Craig, on the other hand, very much did. Lowden, Turner and O’Connor all made perfect sense given this history, while Pattinson, already known to billions for playing Edward Cullen and Batman, brings associative celebrity baggage that Bond has never had to contend with before. Is that a problem? Not necessarily. Director Denis Villeneuve , a high-end, blue-chip blockbuster artist with a distinct stylistic signature, isn’t the typical choice of Bond helmer either — so if he’s going in his own prestigious direction with the series, it makes sense for him to take an equivalently A-list leading man (and one with whom he has an existing relationship, through “Dune: Part Three”) with him. And yet there’s something about the choice, on paper at least, that doesn’t sit right with me. It seems a little too neat, too convenient, even a bit too risk-averse — the proven safe bet taken over the chance to mint a brand-new megastar. I have little doubt that Pattinson, a reliably terrific actor, will make a fine Bond: tall and elegant and angularly handsome, he certainly looks the part and he can project the balance of charm and chill needed to play a character who, in any incarnation, remains a suave killing machine. Is he a little too good for the part, though? Perhaps. Pattinson’s reputation as a movie star rests on playing two darkly brooding mainstream heroes; his reputation as an actor, however, has been considerably enriched by his predilection for playing, frankly, losers and weirdos: a hapless small-time criminal in the Safdie Brothers’ “Good Time”; a deranged, gull-mauling lighthouse keeper in “The Lighthouse”; a sniveling, pathetic read of Chris Hansen in “Primetime”; or whatever the hell he’s doing, multiple times over, in Bong Joon-ho’s loopy sci-fi “Mickey 17.” Even his blockbuster assignments are more interesting when he lets his inner freak out to play: His big, heightened, leeringly villainous turn in “The Odyssey” is off on its own beam entirely. I don’t know that James Bond is really the role to mine Pattinson’s most compelling eccentricities as an actor: The very point of the character, across 25 films, has been that he’s a well-dressed, tightly controlled cipher who has a sharp way with a one-liner. Perhaps Villeneuve and his chosen star have other ideas, but it’s hard to imagine the character straying too far from a failsafe template. One hopes instead that Pattinson is negotiating himself enough time between 007 shoots (and at least one more “The Batman” entry still on the docket) to do the odd auteur projects he clearly loves — and that adventurously chosen collaborators like Claire Denis (“High Life”) and Lynne Ramsay (“Die My Love”) can only benefit from his cachet. In the meantime, spare a thought for the less famous guys who, for a moment there, thought they had a shot at being cinema’s longest-running action man. They’ll all be fine — I confess to some relief in particular that O’Connor, a superb and unusual hybrid of character actor and leading man, may have more time for the intrepid arthouse projects in which he thrives — and will doubtless each get some manner of boost for having been so prominently on the shortlist. The reboot, which combines the gameplay of the original with new twists and a high-stakes Jackpot bonus round, will launch in broadcast syndication in fall 2027 on the CBS Owned Stations. It is unclear yet what the stations will drop for next fall to make room for The Joker’s Wild . After three rounds, the contestant with the most points wins the game. The most recent revival with host Snoop Dogg wan on TBS and TNT for two seasons. The Joker’s Wild is produced by Sony Pictures Television and executive produced by showrunner Mashawn Nix, whose credits include Deal or No Deal, Match Game and Red Table Talk . Ad sales for the series will be handled by CBS Media Ventures. title: Higher Ground’s ‘The Eyes Of Ghana’ Sets Global Release On IShowSpeed’s YouTube Channel
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News New James Bond Found: Robert Pattinson To Play Next 007 Read the full story By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill ‘Club Kid’ Rocks Limited Expansion As ‘Paper Tiger’ Scores James Gray’s Best Per-Screen Debut — Specialty Box Office ‘Victorian Psycho’ Joins New James Gray and Pedro Almodóvar Releases In Indie Weekend Lineup — Specialty Preview ‘Musk’ Director Alex Gibney Calls Midterm Blue Wave “Magnificent” But Warns “Hard Work Has Just Begun” View All November 16, 2026 10:11am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Chris Hesse in 'The Eyes of Ghana' Breakwater Studios/Higher Ground Breakwater Studios and the Obamas’ Higher Ground will stream The Eyes of Ghana on YouTube on November 17 in a novel partnership with social media star IShowSpeed , aka Darren Watkins, who is also a producer on the film. The documentary, directed by Ben Proudfoot and executive produced by President Barack Obama and Michelle Obama, will show on IShowSpeed’s YouTube Channel, which has more than 62 million subscribers worldwide. The awards contender, officially shortlisted for Best Feature Documentary and Best Score at the 42nd IDA Documentary Awards, follows a Ghanaian cameraman’s extraordinary mission to rescue a hidden film archive documenting the birth of African independence. IShowSpeed (known as Speed) shared official trailer on his channels where it received over 3 million views. Related Stories Documentary Kris Bowers On Creating A Love Letter To Ghana & Film History With His Score For 'The Eyes Of Ghana' - Sound & Screen Film News Zainab Johnson Sets Release Date For Netflix Stand-Up Special 'Toxically Optimistic' Marking First From Obamas' Higher Ground The news follows a breakout year for YouTube creators at the box office as well as continuing experimentation by filmmakers and distributors seeking new ways to get their films to audiences directly, in this case collaborating with a streaming creator rather than a traditional streaming platform. Watch on Deadline The doc had a one-day theatrical release, announced by Speed, on October 28 in 100+ theaters in North America, London and Accra, Ghana via Regal, AMC, Cinemark and some indies. He attended the New York premiere showing, livestreaming his arrival. The social media creator, 21, with a total audience of more than 200 million followers across platforms, was named World’s Most Influential Creator by Rolling Stone in 2025 and one of TIME Magazine’s Most Influential Creators in 2026. He also traces his ancestry to Ghana. During his Speed Does Africa tour earlier this year, the creator visited Accra where he told viewers he was “back home.” “To have the opportunity to use my platform to share this history with the world for free is an incredible moment. After visiting Ghana last year and finding out that my family history can be traced back to West Africa, I know how powerful it can be to feel connected to where you come from,” he said. “I’m so grateful to the people of Ghana, to Chris Hesse for preserving these incredible images, to Ben Proudfoot and the filmmaking team for bringing this story to life. To be part of this alongside President Obama and Michelle Obama is an honor of a lifetime” he said. The 90-minute film follows veteran Ghanaian cinematographer Chris Hesse, who served as personal cameraman to Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana’s first president and a leading voice for African liberation. As his eyesight fades, Hesse races against time to rescue more than 1,000 films capturing the continent’s struggle for independence in the 1950s and 60s. Hidden for decades after Nkrumah’s overthrow in a 1966 coup, the archive becomes a bridge between generations to fill in their lost history. Five years ago, after a chance encounter, Hesse asked fellow documentarian Proudfoot to tell his story. “Over six decades ago Chris Hesse picked up a camera and documented one of the most pivotal moments in world history,” says Ethan Lewis, Head of Non-Fiction at Higher Ground. “Now, thanks to iShowSpeed and this historic, precedent setting partnership, this history will be shared for all to see for free.” The Eyes of Ghana opened the TIFF Docs program in 2025 and had its international premiere in competition at the BFI London Film Festival. Its honors include the Special Jury Prize and Best Documentary at the Africa International Film Festival in Lagos, Audience Awards at the Hamptons International and Annapolis Film Festivals, and Heartland Film Festival’s Jimmy Stewart Legacy Award. Cinematographer Brandon Somerhalder ( Come See Me in the Good Light ) shot The Eyes of Ghana across multiple formats, including sequences captured on Imax 65mm film. Original score from Academy Award winner Kris Bowers, Proudfoot’s frequent collaborator. The film is produced by Proudfoot, Nana Adwoa Frimpong, Moses Bwayo, Anita Afonu, Brandon Somerhalder, Ethan Lewis and Vinnie Malhotra. In addition to President Barack Obama and Michelle Obama, executive producers include Sir John Akomfrah, Kofi Amoo-Gottfried, Paula Madison, Dan and Lian Gill, Max Johnson, Jonathan E. Lim, Michael Risley, Josh Rosenberg, David Treatman and Esther Wojcicki. IShowSpeed, was named to the inaugural TIME100 Creators list and ranked No. 1 on Rolling Stone’s 2025 Most Influential Creators list. His honors also include consecutive Streamer of the Year awards in 2024 and 2025. Carr had previously served as BET’s president of media sales but was elevated to president last December while maintaining his media sales role, reporting to George Cheeks, then chair of TV media at Paramount Skydance. Cheeks, now co-chair and chief content officer for Skydance TV , announced the exit on Monday. “I’m deeply grateful to Louis,” Cheeks said in a memo to staff. “For four decades, he has been one of BET’s greatest champions, helping shape the brand, its business and its connection to Black audiences and culture. Cheeks didn’t immediately announce Carr’s replacement, but said “we will have more to share soon on BET leadership and structure.” In his own memo to staff, Carr said: “For 40 years, I have had one of the best jobs in the media and entertainment industry. Having a position that gives one the opportunity to carry out a purpose that is bigger than oneself is a privilege. Working for a brand whose mission from day one was to uplift and empower the Black community is an honor I’ll never forget.” “That said, even as I write this email, I wrestle with my decision that the time has come to make a transition. Based on recent events within our community and our country, I’ve decided to chart a new path and my last day will be December 31.” Besides his four decades at BET, Carr founded the Louis Carr Internship Foundation to help improve diversity in corporate America through paid internships. He also wrote the book “Dirty Little Secrets” and “Little Black Book: Daily Motivations for Business and Personal Growth.” In 2023, Carr was inducted into the Advertising Hall of Fame and received the Chicago Advertising Federation Silver Medal Award. Last year, Mills’ exit came after the acquisition of Paramount Global by David Ellison’s Skydance Media; similarly, Carr’s departure comes following the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. by Skydance. Here is Cheeks’ memo to staff: Hi Team, I wanted to share the note below from Louis Carr, who has decided to leave the company after an extraordinary career at BET. I’m deeply grateful to Louis. George And here is Carr’s memo to BET staffers: Dear Team, For 40 years, I have had one of the best jobs in the media and entertainment industry. Having a position that gives one the opportunity to carry out a purpose that is bigger than oneself is a privilege. Working for a brand whose mission from day one was to uplift and empower the Black community is an honor I’ll never forget. That said, even as I write this email, I wrestle with my decision that the time has come to make a transition. Based on recent events within our community and our country, I’ve decided to chart a new path and my last day will be December 31. BET has never been just a job to me. It has been a community, a culture and a place to serve. When I reflect on this journey, I am incredibly proud of what we have accomplished together. Over the years, we helped transform the multicultural advertising landscape, built meaningful relationships with some of the world’s most recognized brands and served as the launching pad for today’s top Black creators. We demonstrated the undeniable value, influence, and purchasing power of Black consumers while helping companies better understand and invest in our communities. I am particularly proud of the momentum we have created and the work we have undertaken to strengthen the brand, expand our business and reaffirm BET’s place at the center of Black culture. title: ‘The Joker’s Wild’ Game Show Sets Reboot Hosted by Howie Mandel
full_text: × Continue to Variety SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Breaking News Robert Pattinson Is the New James Bond Nov 16, 2026 10:00am PT ‘The Joker’s Wild’ Game Show Sets Reboot Hosted by Howie Mandel By Ethan Shanfeld Plus Icon Ethan Shanfeld @ethanshanfeld Latest ‘The Joker’s Wild’ Game Show Sets Reboot Hosted by Howie Mandel 1 hour ago Elon Musk Criticizes Jeremy Culhane’s ‘SNL’ Impression: ‘They Need to Try Harder’ 3 hours ago ‘Survivor’ Season 52 Premiere Date Set at CBS in Midseason Slate 4 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy Everett Collection “The Joker’s Wild” is coming back again. Howie Mandel will host a reboot of the classic game show, which will begin production in November for a launch in broadcast syndication on CBS Owned Stations in fall 2027. The revival will combine the familiar gameplay of the original program, which debuted in 1972 and was rebooted a couple of times throughout the decades, with new twists and a high-stakes bonus round. Related Stories Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues Two contestants compete by taking spins on the High Roller slot machine and answering trivia questions across different categories. Jokers are, of course, wild, increasing the points up for grabs. After three fast-paced rounds, the contestant with the most points wins the game. That winner moves on to the new Joker’s Jackpot bonus round, where they’ll face tempting deals with the Devil. If they manage to avoid the Devil, they will win a jackpot between $10,000 and $50,000. “I love that we’re bringing ‘The Joker’s Wild’ back,” said Mandel in a statement. “It’s such a fun, crazy show, and getting to be a part of that is a real honor. There’s something great about taking a show people have loved for years and seeing what you can do with it today. I’m excited to get in there, have some laughs, and probably make a little bit of a mess along the way. That’s usually when I’m having the most fun.” Mandel is no stranger to game shows, having hosted “Deal or No Deal” in the 2000s. He is also a longtime judge of “America’s Got Talent” and is the new host of “The Price Is Right Tonight.” “The Joker’s Wild” was created by Jack Barry, who hosted the program until his death in 1984. After the series endured a variety of iterations, it was briefly rebooted in 2017 with host Snoop Dogg. That version ran for two years, meaning the series will have been off the air for eight years by the time the Mandel reboot launches. “‘The Joker’s Wild’ is one of the most recognizable brands in game show history, with a format that combines trivia, unpredictability and big-money stakes,” said Suzanne Prete, president of game shows at Sony Pictures Television. “Howie brings exactly the kind of wit, energy and spontaneity that this game demands. With him at the helm, we’re excited to introduce ‘The Joker’s Wild’ to a new generation of viewers and continue evolving this iconic franchise for today’s audiences without losing the qualities that made it a favorite in the first place.” The series is produced by Sony Pictures Television and executive produced by Mashawn Nix. After years spent bouncing between theater and prestige television, Spector’s turn as railroad baron George Russell on HBO’s The Gilded Age has made him an object of internet lust — “Train Daddy,” to a particularly enthusiastic segment of the show’s fan base — and given him the sort of platform he’s still figuring out what to do with. And now comes an even bigger leap: Spector is taking over as Robert Langdon, the globe-trotting Harvard symbologist Tom Hanks played in three blockbuster movies, in Netflix’s upcoming adaptation of Dan Brown’s The Secret of Secrets . It’s easily the biggest role of Spector’s career. Related Stories TV 'The Gilded Age' Is Serving Up Ambition and Shame in Season 4 Return Movies 'Moonfish' Review: Morgan Spector and Lucy Liu Voice a Spare but Evocative Animated Sci-Fi Suffused With Loneliness Although Spector is quick to qualify the achievement. “But my wife is No. 2,” he says, referring to spouse and Secrets co-star Rebecca Hall. “So I don’t get to eat all the green M&Ms on set, if you know what I mean.” Spector is currently experiencing one of the more interesting midcareer moments in Hollywood. Until relatively recently, he seemed comfortably settled into being one of those reliably excellent performers whose face audiences might recognize even if his name didn’t immediately come to mind. His growing celebrity has presented another complication. “My era of becoming somebody with a platform has also been a time of dramatic political change, and I’m an outspoken person,” Spector says. “Sometimes I’d like to get off social media, but then I’m abandoning a space that I can use to say things that matter. But then, I have to do all the things that make people want to come to the platform, which means taking pretty pictures of yourself. There’s only so much reposting of ‘Democracy Now’ that your average Instagram viewer wants to see.” Morgan Spector Photographed by OK McCausland Morgan Spector Photographed by OK McCausland In the years before The Gilded Age , Spector was doing what actors have traditionally done when nobody was asking them for selfies: looking for work. After graduating from Reed College and the American Conservatory Theater in San Francisco, he moved to New York, where in 2010 a two-line walk-on in the Broadway production of A View From the Bridge turned into a starring role opposite Liev Schreiber and Scarlett Johansson. “I was living off Nostrand Avenue in Brooklyn at the time, and I would commute in to work every day in a state of euphoria,” he says. “It just felt like New York City was wrapping its arms around me and giving me all I’ve ever dreamed of. But then I had to calibrate and think, ‘OK, well, what else is possible now?’ “ For a while, the answer was more work rather than stardom. Roles on Homeland and miniseries The Plot Against America followed, and when Spector auditioned to play George Russell on The Gilded Age , he saw the Julian Fellowes drama as a chance to add another solid credit — and, with any luck, a steady job — to his résumé. “They originally talked about five seasons as being a way to complete the arc,” Spector says. “But I saw that [HBO head of drama] Francesca Orsi say she’d love it to run for 10 years, so who knows?” What he didn’t foresee was the way audiences would respond to George. “Somebody wrote a piece about how George and Bertha’s [Carrie Coon] marriage was the sexiest thing on television, and I remember thinking, ‘What?!’ ” he says with a laugh. “The show is relatively chaste, especially for HBO, and we weren’t really lingering in eroticism. But it was the first sign that, OK, people are connecting to this in a way that wasn’t obvious to us as we were making it.” Then came Robert Langdon. When Spector read for The Secret of Secrets with showrunner Carlton Cuse, he was reminded of his Gilded Age audition — another opportunity he wasn’t entirely sure made sense for him. “I didn’t think I was right for the part, and I guess as I’m getting older, I’m realizing that I don’t know what’s going to work for me or what I’m going to be good at,” Spector adds with a laugh. He is now filming The Secret of Secrets in Prague. The acting part, at least, he knows how to handle. The rest of his newfound celebrity is proving more complicated. “They don’t teach you about this part in school,” he says. “It’s like, how many thirst traps are enough and how many are too many? We’re making our way through the wilderness.” Morgan Spector Photographed by OK McCausland Morgan Spector Photographed by OK McCausland Spector in HBO’s The Gilded Age. title: Shondaland Taps Amy Joy Rivkin and Karyn Smith-Forge for Key Executive Roles
full_text: × Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All November 16, 2026 9:28am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Amy Joy Rivkin and Karyn Smith-Forge Courtesy Shondaland (2) Shondaland is adding to its executive ranks. The production company founded by Shonda Rhimes and Betsy Beers has named Amy Joy Rivkin as vp production and Karyn Smith-Forge as vp scripted series. Rivkin comes to Shondaland from Media Res, and Smith-Forge from Don Cheadle’s production company This Radicle Act. “Amy Joy’s impressive track record steering complex, premium productions and Karyn’s vast experience and sharp instincts across scripted genres make them powerful additions to Shondaland,” said Alison Eakle, Shondaland’s chief content officer. “We’re thrilled we get to shape our next chapter of storytelling alongside them.” Related Stories TV Shonda Rhimes Signs New Overall Deal at Netflix TV Kim Raver on Leaving 'Grey's Anatomy': "Who Gets to Play a Character for This Long?" Rivkin will oversee physical production on Shondaland’s shows, which include Netflix’s Bridgerton , ABC’s Grey’s Anatomy and its upcoming spinoff and a number of projects in development. She spent the past four years at The Morning Show and Pachinko producer Media Res. Prior to that, she was at Netflix, handling production management for the streamer’s original drama series, and Legendary Entertainment. As vp scripted series, Smith-Forge will lead development of new series from Shondaland at Netflix, where the company has a rich overall deal. Smith-Forge was most recently president of This Radicle Act, working with Cheadle on TV and film projects at a number of outlets, including Netflix, Showtime, AMC, FX and HBO Max. She was previously senior vp production at Berlanti Productions, where she managed a slate of some 20 series, including The CW’s Arrow -verse. THR

Hull is launching StoryMath with Steven Lilien and Bryan Wynbrandt, who created CBS’ God Friended Me . This comes after Hull signed with Range Media Partners . StoryMath will be behind an English-language adaptation of The Innocent , based on Coben’s eponymous 2005 book, which was previously adapted by Netflix into a Spanish-language series in 2021. The U.S. version is set up at Netflix with Coben’s company Final Twist also producing. Related Stories Agencies Penn Badgley Signs With WME & Range Media Partners Agencies Range Media Partners Signs Filmmaker Dexter Fletcher The production company will also be repped by Range and CAA, which both now rep the trio. Watch on Deadline Hull is becoming quite the creative partner for prolific author Coben, who has an overall deal with Netflix. He created, serves as showrunner and is exec producing I Will Find You , which is due out on the streamer later this year. The series marks the first Coben project greenlit out of the U.S. , rather than previous shows, which have come out of the UK. Currently in post-production, it follows an innocent father serving life for the murder of his own son, who receives evidence that his child may still be alive—and must break out of prison to find out the truth. It stars Sam Worthington, Britt Lower, Milo Ventimiglia, Erin Richards, Logan Browning, Jonathan Tucker and Chi McBride. Hull previously served as co-showrunner and exec producer on God Friended Me , the Brandon Micheal Hall-led series that ran for two seasons on CBS. Other credits including NBC’s Quantum Leap , Fox’s Gotham and Alcatraz , ABC’s Once Upon A Time and The CW’s Gossip Girl and Veronica Mars. Hull also continues to be repped by Felker Toczek Suddleson McGinnis Ryan LLP, while Lilien and Wynbrandt are also repped by Yorn, Levine, Barnes, Krintzman, Rubenstein, Kohner, Endlich, Goodell & Gellman. While not as flashy as some of Netflix’s marquee franchises as Bridgerton or Stranger Things , the adaptations of his bestselling thrillers have become a cottage industry, delivering high volume and solid return on investment. Then there are big breakouts, such as Fool Me Once and, most recently , I Will Find You starring Sam Worthington, Netflix’s first American Harlan Coben adaptation. Extending its streak at the top of Netflix’s weekly Top 10 English series rankings to five consecutive weeks — the first series to do it since Wednesday Season 2 — I Will Find You collected 7.3 million views during the week of July 20 to become Netflix’s biggest original scripted debut of 2026. Kelley A Go As Streamer Extends Deal With Harlan Coben With that, the tally for the limited series, which has hit #1 in 81 countries, has gone up to 101.9 million total views to make Netflix’s Most Popular English Series list, bumping fellow 2026 thriller limited series His & Hers (98.2M) from the No.10 spot. Watch on Deadline And with I Will Find You just over a third into the qualifying 91-day viewership window, the series is well positioned to climb further up the list by several slots. Under Netflix’s partnership with the prolific author, the streamer has released 13 series adaptations of Coben novels to date made across multiple countries, with more underway — including a show based on the Myron Bolitar books headlined by Colin Woodell. I Will Find You became the second series to make Netflix’s Most Popular List after the 2024 Fool Me Once held the No. 10 spot for awhile with 98M views over 91 days. “Harlan is brilliant, he really understands his audience, we’ve had so much success, and I Will Find You is very much tracking to be up there,” Netflix’s Head of UCAN Scripted Series Jinny Howe told Deadline earlier this month when the series was on its way to crack the Most Popular list. “We’re very proud of its performance, it continues to be successful and watched around the world.”

title: New James Bond Found: Robert Pattinson To Play Next 007
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News New James Bond Found: Robert Pattinson To Play Next 007 Read the full story By Justin Kroll Justin Kroll Film Editor @krolljvar More Stories By Justin New James Bond Found As Amazon MGM Studios Taps Robert Pattinson To Play Next 007 Aaron Pierre And ‘Sisu’ Director Jalmari Helander Team on Action Thriller ‘Fairytale In New York’ From Netflix And Lionsgate Margot Robbie & Kristoffer Borgli Team On ‘The Week Of Pain’ From A24 And Square Peg View All November 16, 2026 7:01am Add us as a Google Preferred Source After a long and thorough search, Amazon MGM Studios has found its next James Bond as Robert Pattinson has landed the coveted role in the next installment in the hit spy franchise. Following the last round of screen tests that Deadline first reported at the end of October, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Denis Villeneuve landed on the Primetime star to lead the franchise for Amazon MGM Studios. Related Stories Actors Who Have Played James Bond: Sean Connery To Daniel Craig News James Bond Movies In Order: Filmography, Bond Women & Iconic Villains The news was announced on the 007 Instagram account: View this post on Instagram The process to find the next 007 goes back to the spring, when the studio announced casting director Nina Gold was joining the project and that the search was underway. Following two months of meetings, Deadline reported the first round of auditions would take place in August; since then, the studio, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Villeneuve cut the list to its final group and worked out test offers in September. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime. I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team,” said Pattinson. Watch on Deadline The final tests were originally planned for earlier in October, but due to schedule conflicts with the finalists, were pushed to the end of the month so they could happen around the same time. While not confirmed sources say the group was no bigger than five actors with Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Nicholas Hoult and Josh O’Connor among the others who would end up testing. Once those were finished, producers and execs took their time with making a decision, ultimately landing on Pattinson for the role. With the process of finding Bond now behind them, producers will now look to fill out the remaining cast members which include a new Bond Lady, the villain, as well as the roles of M and Q. As for Pattinson, when news broke that he was one of the five names, many were quite surprised given that he not only was an established star but already had a major franchise under his belt with The Batman. As the weeks have passed since the initial tests, producers and the studio wanted at least one major star in the mix and it also seemed obvious to most that Pattinson was very interested in tackling another high-profile role. As for his role as the Caped Crusader, Pattinson is currently finishing the final weeks of production on The Batman Part II , which should wrap before end of the year. Before landing Bond, Pattinson was on quite the heater starring in several films including the A24 pic The Drama, Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey and Primetime with Dune Part III bowing next month. He is repped by WME and 3 Arts Entertainment.
